sources.title: Revelation 13, text and explanatory notes

sources.title: 1 John 2

sources.title: 1 John 4

sources.title: 2 Thessalonians 2

sources.title: Daniel 7

sources.title: Isaiah 45

sources.title: Malachi 4

sources.title: What Is the Jewish Belief About Moshiach (Messiah)?

sources.note: Describes a potentially qualified person in each generation. Potentiality is not completed fulfillment, and the article does not establish one reincarnating individual or a messiah for every contemporary nation.

sources.title: Mishneh Torah, Kings and Wars, chapter 11

frameworks.name: Historical referent / reception
frameworks.question: What did a text mean in its initial setting, or how was it later applied?
frameworks.distinction: An ancient referent, a later political image and a present comparison are different claims.

frameworks.name: Specific future fulfillment
frameworks.question: Does the interpreter propose a particular final figure or sequence?
frameworks.distinction: Keep the specified events, actors and conditions intact. A recurring metaphor is not automatically this claim.

frameworks.name: Recurring or distributed pattern
frameworks.question: Can a role recur across people, generations and institutions?
frameworks.distinction: This is a theological reading. Recurrence does not establish literal possession or one migrating supernatural individual.

frameworks.name: Inward transformation
frameworks.question: What changes in the reader's understanding, conduct and relation to the world?
frameworks.distinction: The Gospel of Philip offers a living-resurrection comparison; it does not establish a single belief of all Gnostics or remove outward catastrophe from consideration.

frameworks.name: Potential Messiah in each generation
frameworks.question: How does this tradition distinguish potentiality from accomplishment?
frameworks.distinction: A tradition-specific expectation is not a verified designation of a current leader and does not by itself assert reincarnation.

frameworks.name: Distinct messianic / prophetic offices
frameworks.question: Which texts distinguish priest, king, prophet or other anointed roles?
frameworks.distinction: Multiple offices are not interchangeable titles or automatic proof of multiple simultaneous national messiahs.

frameworks.name: Modern analogy / open author proposal
frameworks.question: What comparison is being proposed, without a demonstrated identity?
frameworks.distinction: Retain the proposal and its author. Do not report it as a recovered ancient prediction or independent endorsement.

method.title: What one row means
method.text: A row preserves one attributed interpretation or reception-history record. It is not a verdict about a person. One source can discuss several people without becoming several independent witnesses.

method.title: No person scores or standings
method.text: There are no likelihoods, weights, match percentages, leaderboards or scores for public figures. Sorts organize records by name, date or source. Documentary status describes access to material, not a person's moral or political standing.

method.title: Words, events and interpretations
method.text: Keep the original wording or a precise paraphrase, a dated public event, the proposed textual connection, the source's framework and the unresolved inference in separate fields. Where a verse is only an editorial locator, say so.

method.title: Patterns do not erase particulars
method.text: A recurring-role interpretation and a specific fulfillment claim may coexist in an author's work. Neither should silently replace the other. The proposed Agent Smith / successive builds analogy illustrates recurrence, not evidence of possession. An inward transformation reading need not deny external events.

method.title: Identity and stereotypes
method.text: No inference is made from Jewish identity, ethnicity, nationality, ancestry, physical appearance or technology employment to wrongdoing or a supernatural identity. Theological lineage criteria belong to the named tradition, not a generic political test.

method.title: Unknown is not a negative result
method.text: An empty matrix cell means no claim for that person and passage is included in this edition. It does not establish absence, innocence, guilt, mismatch or confirmation. Unverified means the underlying record has not been checked.

method.title: Dates preserve uncertainty
method.text: Claim dates, event dates and retrieval dates are different. Empty dates stay unknown. A year-only label is not silently converted to a precise day. A current webpage is not proof that the same text existed on an earlier day.

method.title: Local work is not publication
method.text: Personal notes are saved only in this browser when storage is available. JSON exports can back them up. Importing or editing notes does not update GitHub or shared records. The supplied files do not publish themselves.
